So cooperation between the civilian and the military judicial organs was discussed at the meeting; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I do not remember it being discussed, unless they had a separate meeting and they had a different meeting. But at this meeting, I do not remember this cooperation discussed. But perhaps there were some separate meetings and perhaps they discussed it at that meeting, and we, the wardens of penitentiaries and reformatories, discussed the rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Just returning very briefly to the Red Cross, Mr. Krnojelac. On the day that the Red Cross finally was allowed to come to the KP Dom on the 23rd of June, 1993, a group of detainees were hidden in the bakery, where they weren't doing any work, but they were simply kept there so they would not be registered; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I do not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: As far as you know, none of the detainees were approved to work at the bakery, right, the group that was hidden that day, including intellectuals such as Safet Avdic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told you that I am not aware of that and that I know nothing about it at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, you were among the people whom the military command included in their list of people who needed to be notified about military arrest authorities; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You were notified that there had been a change in military arrest authorities; right? The military officials notified you of changes in their arrest authority; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No info. I never received -- I was never notified about any military authority or any -- I never received any notification about anything from the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have you shown Exhibit D54.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: This is an order dated 7 September 1992, and it's signed by the Commander of the Foca Tactical Group, Colonel Marko Kovac. And it states that the commander of the military police and chief of security are authorised to arrest an offender at the request of a unit commander, or based on their own assessment, and it also talks about when a person could be released under those circumstances. And under number 3 of this order, it states: "Inform the warden of the Foca KP Dom of this order." That was you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I am telling you that I never had this order and that this has absolutely nothing to do with me, with this order. "Inform the warden of the Foca KP Dom," and above it, it says who can arrest and who can release. So it shows: "Inform the warden of the Foca KP Dom," and who was the warden of the KP Dom in the civilian part, but this then has to do with the warden of the KP Dom responsible for detainees, that same commander or one of his men whom he had authorised to do it, not for me. This has nothing to do with me, because I had no right either to arrest or to release, because you see who arrests and who releases and who has the right to put somebody under arrest.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. We're done with this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, I want to talk about Savo Todovic. When you arrived at the KP Dom, he was already there; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I did not see him there straight away. On the 18th, I did not see him. I do not know even if I saw him on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But later on I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know when he started working there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly about anyone except myself. All I know is that people did not come to the KP Dom right away. The inflow of these workers for the labour duty started somewhere after the 20th, 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You knew that Savo Todovic was somebody who had worked at the KP Dom before the war; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt afterwards, gradually, who had worked where. Before I went there and before this information, I did not know that Savo Todovic used to work for the KP Dom. I learnt about that afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You learned, while you were still working at KP Dom, that Savo Todovic had worked there before the war; right? He was one of the professional staff who returned to the KP Dom as part of his work obligation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I learned that he had worked at the KP Dom before the armed conflict broke out as well, but I don't think that he had work obligation. If you have a document of that kind -- but no, he did not have work obligation; he had a military obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you said "later." It was still while you were at the KP Dom; right? You learned while you were still at the KP Dom that Savo Todovic had worked there before?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the KP Dom, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you also knew that he had been in charge or had been working with legal affairs before the war; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody from amongst the staff at the accounting department told me that he was a clerk who was responsible for convicted persons at first, and later on he became a lawyer. That's what I heard towards the end of my tenure there, and that he became a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: His office was also down the hall from yours, right, on the same floor?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On opposite ends with regard to the staircase, to the left and to the right, but it's on the same floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You also had contact with him regarding the allocation of detainees for work in the economic units; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, may I just explain this? This office was -- after Mr. Vujovic -- or rather, while Mr. Vujovic was there, he was in that office; and later, when Vujovic left the KP Dom, then Mr. Todovic moved to that office. That was -- I can't remember exactly, but let me say that it was almost towards the end of 1992 when Vujovic left. I don't know whether it was September, August. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: For the Court's information, Mr. Vujovic is listed as number 1 on Exhibit P3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic was the lawyer at the KP Dom, right, and when he was there he was also under work obligation; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When Mr. Vujovic left, Mr. Todovic moved into his office, right, and was also working with legal affairs as a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he immediately moved, I don't know, but he was not involved in legal affairs as far as the economic part was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You also knew that Savo Todovic kept a log or files of the convicted prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that. Actually, as far as I know, not all the files of convicted persons at the KP Dom have been found at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The question was about what Savo Todovic was doing at the KP Dom. You told the investigators of the Office of the Prosecution, on the 6th of June, when you spoke, on page 8: "I do not know exactly what Todovic did there. He was not a craftsman or anything like that. He was a lawyer, and he might have done these legal things." Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that I was quite accurate and fair when I said before this Court what he did approximately and what he was in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: On that same page, you said: "Who would know who was under whose supervision?" This is regarding Mr. Todovic still. "I never tasked him with anything. The only thing I knew he did was keeping the log or the files of the convicted prisoners." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war that he did that, yes. As for later on, I think I was quite clear when I talked about this here, and I don't see why you're asking me to repeat all of that, because then we went into closed session when I said to this Honourable Court what he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'd like to have you shown Exhibit D -- I'm sorry, P46. And this is a transcript of the section that I just read out, page 8 as well in the B/C/S. We've put an arrow at the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Krnojelac can just have it placed in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And we've put an arrow at the relevant section, and I'd just like to have it confirmed, that statement that I read, where you stated: "The only thing I knew he did was keeping the log or the files of the convicted persons."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I certainly said here that this was done before the war. Perhaps I didn't say it, but that's what I meant, the work that he did before the war. And later on, I could not have said something like that, like what I said before this Court, perhaps for some justified reasons. And I also said that he was not a craftsman, a repairman, so that he would be in charge of a work unit. He didn't do that before either. And then this was some kind of precaution on my part, because I did not think that questions would be put as to what other people did. I thought that I was only supposed to answer in respect of what did I and what I was in charge of. However, it seems to me that I was clear and accurate in terms of saying before this Honourable Court what I knew. And after all, that is the oath I took, that I will say the truth, and indeed I spoke the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, the section that we're discussing was something you said in answer to the following question: "But was he under your supervision?" So the time that we're talking about was not before the war. You're not talking about what Mr. Todovic did before the war, were you? The question was about your supervision of him, and your answer was about what he did while you were there, and that was to keep a log or files of the convicted persons; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have been trying to find what my learn friend has been saying just now. Could she just tell me, please, on page 8 of the B/C/S version, which line is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: It's toward the bottom of the page, if my memory serves me right, and if counsel would like, we can put that back on the ELMO so he doesn't have to search for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, because I don't seem to be able to find it on page 8 at all.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just say here, in respect of this answer, it says here, in fact, I did not know what he did, and I think that that is the gist of my answer. In fact, I do not know what he did, which means that in that case, I did not say --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, my colleague has shown this to us now, but could she please just tell me where files or a log is mentioned of convicted persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps if you'd just stop talking for a minute, all of you, because the usher was about to put it on the ELMO. It might be a good idea if somebody from the Prosecution could point it out whilst on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. I think Mr. Bakrac is right. We seem to have gotten the wrong page. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You're working from the English version. Have you got the reference in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I have the reference as being page 8 as well, but I think it's inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Because looking at it now, the people who are speaking are not -- they don't match up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So with apologies to the Court, we're going to look for that right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And then perhaps Ms. Dicklich can point it out whilst it's on the ELMO so that Mr. Bakrac can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: While this is being done, Your Honour, I can go on so we don't waste time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Is it going to take very long to find? Surely it is to be found in a paragraph which starts with some words, and if those words can be located, then you should find the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've found it right now. It starts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How about putting a ring around the word, putting it on the ELMO and then Mr. Bakrac can find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: It starts at the bottom of page 7 and it goes to the top of page 8. So the question is at the bottom of page 7, the last line, and then the relevant portion is lines 1 through 3 of page 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that should be sufficient. Have you found it now, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Good. You proceed, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Looking at the bottom of page 7, and there is the question which Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff poses to you: "But was he under your supervision?" And then the answer you gave is on the next page, at the top, and there you said: "Who would know? Who would know who was under whose supervision? I never tasked him with anything. The only thing I knew he did was keeping the log or the files of the convicted persons." Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. And I think you can see this quite well. Who would know who was under whose supervision, when I did not know under whose supervision he was? At that moment, perhaps I did not even have the strength to say that which I was not certain that somebody else would corroborate, too, in terms of what he did. Because it would have been pointless if I was the only person to say before this Honourable Court that somebody had been doing something unless it had been said by someone else too. I think that you should try to understand me on this point, that at that moment, I wanted there to still be some secrecy with regard to what he did. I did not give him any orders. So he did work on this file before the armed conflict, but in this case, no, he had some specific, special tasks that we already said to the Honourable Court here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, are you telling us that during those four days of interviews last year, when you were given the opportunity to say that everything you wanted to, that you kept some things secret?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in all of this, I kept saying the military, the military, the military, but before this Honourable Court, when I testified, I gave the names. So it is true that names were not named then and that no particular reference was made to who was exactly what, except for what was corroborated later by statements of both one and the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: My question to you is: "Did you deliberately withhold information during these four days of interviews? Did you deliberately not state a fact that you're testifying to now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought then that I was only answering with respect to what had to do with me personally and that you and the Court would not be asking me about the work of others. That is why I thought it was sufficient if I would just say what I did and what I was in charge of, because this is my first time in court. I was never before a court of law before, and I don't know what I'm supposed to do. I thought it was sufficient to talk only about my duties, what I did, and what I reported about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your lawyers were there with you during these interviews every single moment; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were present during these interviews, yes. Not at every moment. When they went to have breakfast, they weren't there, but they were present during the interviews, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you were told by the investigator himself, before you began the interview, that if you didn't want to answer questions, you had a right to say you didn't want to answer the question; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. As a matter of fact, he cautioned me that everything that I would say would be held against me. And then I said it would be best for me to keep silent and not to say anything. But then they told me, well, then there would be no point in this kind of an interview. So it was said to me. I was made aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you did answer questions voluntarily; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Voluntarily at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you spoke with the investigators because you felt the need to explain your situation, and you tried to convince them that you were not guilty of what you were accused of; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, I think I once said, "It seems to me that you want to accuse me of something that I have not done, and I'm not going to make any further reference to that."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And had you not wanted to answer a particular question, you were free to say, "I don't wish to answer that question. Please move on"; right? Nobody ever said, "You must answer this question."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the members told me that I could do it that way. However, teachers have an occupational obsession. They speak all the time. And you can see it here, and you have been seeing it, that I talk too much all the time. I want to explain my truth as best I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And are you telling us that in the course of explaining your truth over those four days there was information that you deliberately held back, to keep a secret? Is that what you're telling us? And now today in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. court you're saying that there was further situation?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could not put it that way, to deliberately withhold, to hold back. I thought that it only had to do with me personally, and with the extent to which I am a war criminal in that respect, to present the truth. The truth doesn't always have to be cheerful. It can be happy; it can be sad. But what I wanted to do was to tell the truth, irrespective of what it was like.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, this transcript shows the second day of your interviews. By the time you were asked about Savo Todovic, you had already been asked about several other people at the KP Dom; isn't that right? This was not the first time that you were being asked about someone else's actions.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I even know that I said to the gentlemen, the investigators who talked to me, "Please, I cannot" -- or did I say, "Shall I not mention the name of the person who was present when the Red Cross was there?" Because I hoped that these records, minutes of the Red Cross would be presented to this Honourable Court and that then they would show that such-and-such a person was there on behalf of the military and let him talk about the detained persons. I did not mention that name because I was hoping that his name would be found in the minutes of the Red Cross, this International Red Cross, this humanitarian organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you were asked specific questions about Savo Todovic, you never said, "I don't wish to discuss this person," did you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what could have been said? And which was, in a way, in my opinion, important, I said that already then. I did not say everything, probably. And that is why I later asked for a closed session to say this, because I told you: Foca is a small town. And in addition to that, 19 members of my family -- I mean, I love them, and I have to defend and safeguard the truth as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to page 7, just to go back a little bit further and discuss how this discussion came about during the course of the interview. Go toward the bottom of page 7, please. You were basically going through the list P3, a list of all the employees at the KP Dom, and you've gotten to number -- you went through number 9 or so, and you got to the name Savo Todovic at the very bottom of the page. You point to the middle of that paragraph. You said, "This person, Savo Todovic, it says here he was a deputy chief, a deputy director for legal and financial affairs since 1st July 1993. What he was doing there, I don't know. I only remember that laws were changing in the justice. Most probably that is when this law was changed, that is, when this title of deputy director for legal and financial affairs was introduced, because I do not know of such a name, of such a title." And then you were asked whether Savo Todovic was under your supervision, and then you gave the answer that we quoted earlier. At no point when his name came up on the list and in the course of discussion did you ever say, "I do not wish to speak about this particular individual," isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I said that, I really can't remember. Well, you're showing me this now, but this assistant over here for administrative and financial affairs, appointed as of the 1st of July, 1993, that is on that list of personnel. And already on the 1st of July, 1993, I was being relieved of my duty as warden. At one of the meetings in Bijeljina, mention was made of amending laws in the justice system, and then the name was mentioned of the kind of person who did not exist until then, according to law, that is to say, assistant warden for legal affairs, and in the previous law there was no such post. And when I was told, "Milorad, why are you not talking about this law?" And I said that had it been the law on elementary school, I would talk about it, but since this is the law on justice, I cannot discuss it at all, because I don't know about it, and I certainly won't with be working in the justice system, but I will be working in schools. Because this was in 1973. It was in April or perhaps even May. Then this law about the judiciary was discussed. Because I did not take part in this discussion at all, as I was not very knowledgeable with regard to such matters, and I said that if we were discussing the law on elementary education, I would take part in the discussion, but I would not be needing this because I would not be working at the judiciary. Oh, I do apologise. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: We don't need for you to answer things that are irrelevant, and we certainly don't need for you to repeat that. My question to you was simply about the interview. During the course of the interview, you never once said, "I do not wish to speak about Savo Todovic, because I wish to protect my family or myself or any other person," right? You spoke freely about this person; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is true that I said that Savo Todovic was appointed for military obligation. It is sure that I said that, that he was a military conscript and that he was appointed with regard to military obligation, not work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You stated further - and perhaps with the help of the usher, we can look at the middle of page 8 - when you were asked about whether in fact he was your deputy, and you said he was not. And then, about halfway down the page, you make the following comment: "Anybody in the KP Dom could believe that I was the director of the KP Dom because of their lack of information. Whether he was playing some other game behind my back, as many could have done at KP Dom at that time, starting from the security personnel, I do not know. When I left KP Dom, I found out some things which I did not know while I was there." Here you make reference to some games that could have been played behind your back. Are you saying that Savo Todovic and other security personnel were playing games, pretending that you were in charge when you weren't?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any one of them, either security personnel or any other military person, could have said to everyone, "Well, Milorad is warden of the KP Dom. Milorad is responsible for you." He could have. It doesn't mean to say that he did say it, but he could have, and that is why I said that he could have said something like that behind my back. These are experienced people. They could have said, "It is Milorad's fault that you are detained and everything." I didn't hear that, but he could have said, "Milorad Krnojelac is the warden for everything, but Milorad Krnojelac said what he was and what the military was."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, isn't it true that a year ago, during the time you gave these four days of interviews, you denied knowing who was in charge of the military part of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the army was responsible for the military part, and I did not say who was made responsible on behalf of the army. And to this day, I still do not know -- I wouldn't say exactly, but on the basis of some actions, one could know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Let me see if I heard this correctly. You're saying to this very day, you don't know who was in charge of the military part of the KP Dom, the counterpart to the civilian side, of which you were in charge?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm only referring to this transcript before a year ago, and I say: Well, today one already knows these things, and at that time it was the way it was. If a document is adopted by somebody else, and if it is not adopted by Milorad Krnojelac, then it means that the other person is responsible and not Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, let me quote to you from the 6th of June. This is Exhibit P46, and it's page 4 in both the B/C/S and the English: "I wish I had known then who the director of the other unit was. I only know that it was a military unit belonging to the Tactical Group in Velecevo." You said that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, let me tell you something. Honestly, I was under no oath at that time, and I consider this conversation with gentlemen from the Office of the Prosecutor was something completely else from how I understood that the purpose of this Tribunal. I thought I was talking with them about those situations which had to do with me. And at that moment I never talked about that other part which I simply -- but what Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. referred simply to the military command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo, the accused has said several times that his belief was they were only interested in what he was doing. Are you going to investigate that at all? Was he told not to talk about other people, or what?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It seems to me that you've let it go each time. If you're going to take it up later, by all means. I don't want to take your cross-examination out of order. But it is a surprising assertion which it seems to be needed to be investigated, at least a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. I'll do that right now, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, are you saying that you were told that you would only be giving information about yourself and not be asked questions about other people?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right now I can't remember whether this is correct. I was asked about others. I cannot deny that. But my idea was that it will be enough to only speak about what I did and what I knew in this particular case, and what I was responsible for. I simply never thought that I should then speak about who else did what and what his duty was. That was my line of thinking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Surely you expected that if you were trying to say someone else was responsible, that you would be asked who that other person was in order for you to assert your innocence; right? That certainly came as no surprise to you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came as a surprise to me that nobody was ready to understand me that I was not responsible, and that is what I was explaining, that I was responsible for something else and not for the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Sir, the question was not related to your actions. You've already told us that. The question was related to whether you logically would have expected that someone would be interested in who was responsible, if not you; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even one of the members of that team conducting the interview said, "Don't explain to us. Don't explain to us. If you don't want to mention somebody, just tell us, 'I don't want to speak about that.'" In other words, it was enough for me to talk about myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And in the passage we just went through, you never said, "I don't wish to speak about this individual," right? You went ahead and said what you knew about that person, and it certainly didn't include his being in charge of the military part; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of all that I said, that he was a military conscript, and it was a common fact that he was responsible for the military part not for the economic part, because it was not a labour duty; it was military duty. And I thought that it was enough for me to say that, to point out that. Because my knowledge of law, excuse me, but is really none, because I know nothing about it, and then here I'm confronted with all that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, you stated earlier, just a few minutes ago, that at the time that you made this statement to the investigators, that you were not under oath. Are you telling us that because you were not under oath, you did not tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heaven forbid. I spoke the truth then, except that I didn't mention directly the work tasks of other people, because my motive is truth, nothing but the truth, and I think I said somewhere I want to defend myself with truth, even though some others maybe do not want to testify to that. I don't know which part of the transcript that is in.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And the passage I've quoted to you just now where you said: "I wish I had known then who the director of the other unit was, that is, the director of the military part," that's accurate; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can interpret it as you like and say that that is correct, but I can say that I simply did not know that I was supposed to say, "Well, that is so-and-so," even on that occasion. But I think it's never late to arrive at the truth, and I've repeated it now during my testimony before this Honourable Court. Because usually one says the truth is like the cork. The deeper you try to sink it, it will surface sooner or later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I would like to show you this transcript so we have a better idea of the context in which this statement arose. It's Exhibit P46, and it's page 4 in the English, and it's also page 4 in the B/C/S. In the English it's line 5. The question that was posed to you was: "I really want to know who was the warden at the time that you were there as the head of the economic part of the KP Dom." And the answer that you gave is at the bottom of the page. We're having it highlighted right now. This is the question that's being posed to you, which I've just read out, regarding who was the warden. Your answer to that was not, "I don't wish to answer this."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher can leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read it. I haven't read it yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your answer to that question: "Who was the warden of the KP Dom if you were the director of the economic unit?" was not, "I don't wish to answer that," but it was, rather: "I wish I knew, too, and I wish I had known then who the director of the other unit was. I only know that it was the military unit belonging to the Tactical Group in Velecevo." So you affirmatively say that you don't know; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My -- my answer was that that is the Tactical Group which was at Velecevo and was under the military command. And you can see straight away here that it was the warden of that same technical group or, rather, from the military command and that at that time I didn't quote his full name. Now, again, the commander was so-and-so, and now I think in this case if he was the commander, then he was also the warden of that military part, because it doesn't say anywhere the warden of the military part but the commander of the Tactical Group, and it was all subordinated to the military command. Therefore, the warden is most probably the commander of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So my point is you simply said you didn't know the name and now you wish to tell us that you do know the name; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, somewhere during the interview, I mentioned the name of Mr. Marko Kovac. I hope that you will find it somewhere in the transcript, because I did mention his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, it's a fact, isn't it, that during your interviews, you were not afraid to give names. You were simply asserting to this one single point that you didn't know what the name was; right? You never said you were afraid and didn't want to give the name. You simply said you didn't know who it was; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that there was no need for me to mention any names, and I am telling you because I don't know how else to answer these questions. I simply thought there was no need for me to mention their names and that I should speak only about my part, that is, what I did and what I was in charge of. And if that is a mistake and if that is a responsibility, then it is up to the Honourable Court to think about it. I'm telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have the witness shown the transcript from the last day of the interview, which is the 27th of July. The Exhibit number is P50. The relevant page is 21 in the English, and the B/C/S is now being shown on the ELMO. If we could move it up just a little. Yes, a little bit so that we can see the beginning of that. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You were asked by Mr. Kemppainen: "So my last question was about military command, the chain of command in military, and who was responsible for the military part of the KP Dom? And if I got it right, you are not willing to give in the names. And for further clarification, KP Dom and military in general. Yes, the military part. I mean the military part." And then your answer, Mr. Krnojelac: "It's not that I don't want to give names, it's just that I don't know who was in charge there." Those are your words; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it did not happen in the KP Dom, in the administrative building where I was. It happened in the military command. That is, I insisted on drawing these distinctions and that is why I am supplementing this answer. I meant the military part of the KP Dom. Then -- and that is what the gentleman said. And then I answer it's not that I don't want to, it's that I do not know who was responsible for it all, because it did not happen in the KP Dom, in the administrative building where I was, but it was settled in the army command, which means that I did not have an opportunity to see what went on in the army command, and in that case -- and it didn't happen in the administrative building where I worked and where I performed my duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, you've talked very much about this division between the military part and the civilian part, and you've made reference to this contract letting the military use a part of the KP Dom. Isn't it true that you personally were the person who permitted the military to take, to rent out part of the KP Dom for their use?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not do that of my own will, but excuse me, just recall that I said that on the 19th, with Mr. Mladjenovic, the President of the Excessive Board of the Assembly of the municipality of Foca, who said himself that that matter would be settled. And that matter was then settled, and it seems to me that I -- well, we've been talking now, you and I, for a long time, but I think I've told you that. And when that letter arrived, then I asked him, "So what do I do now?" And that -- because he was the only one nearby whom I could ask. And he said, "Well, Milorad, there is no more convenient place or better place for those people than the KP Dom, and so approve it." And I just approved it and told him that they should return it in a proper state, in the working order, because I thought it would be all over much sooner. I never thought that these armed conflicts would go on until the Dayton Accords in 1995. I thought it will be over much sooner than that. It will be over in a couple of days and that that part would not be needed, that it would all be exchanged, that the people would go back to their homes and their families and I back to my job and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have the witness shown D38.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: This is a request directed to the KP Dom Foca from the Commander of the Foca Tactical Group, signed Miro Stanic. And just by the way, Miro Stanic is the same person you've identified already as the President of the SDS from that list of Crisis Staff members; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Miro Stanic's signature. At least that's what it says in the typewriter. What is it in handwriting, I don't know, but it says Miro Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So this is dated the 8th of May, 1992, and you saw that document; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So actually, in addition to being the President of the SDS, Miro Stanic -- you already knew at that point that Miro Stanic was also the Commander of the Foca Tactical Group during this time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he was the commander of the Tactical Group I didn't know, but it says here the "Commander of the Tactical Group," and I cannot say yes or no, because with the army, I don't know their positions. But it says the "Commander of the Tactical Group." Whether he was the commander or not, I do not know that. But it says here the commander. Excuse me, "For the commander." If I'm correct, here on the stamp it says, "For." Oh, yes. I saw this "a" and dash, and that is why I understand it must be for the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that convention which is --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you don't see it in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When it says "For" it usually means that somebody else is signing it but that it's on behalf of another person, usually a much higher-ranking person; right? That's what it means?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that he's not the commander, that it's for, for. It means on behalf of the commander. That's how I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: On behalf of the Commander Miro Stanic; right? The title "commander" belongs to Miro Stanic, right? Because both names are typed -- both the title and the name are typed in, even if the signature may not be the same person; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, it says here "Miro Stanic," typewritten and signed for the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll just take a look, a quick look at the B/C/S version so that everybody understands this discussion, which the witness has. Very briefly, if the witness could place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The word "commander" is written in -- is typed in, and the name "Miro Stanic" is also typed in; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Except that it is this dash and "a," written by hand. And on this stamp, I suppose it also says "for."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes: That is, the word "Za," Za, which means "for" or "on behalf of," and the "a" is the accusative.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: But you're saying that Miro Stanic was not, in fact, the commander but that as President of the SDS he was signing on behalf of somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that. I'm not claiming that either he was or that he wasn't, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Let's take it then as either possibility. Mr. Stanic was either the Commander of the Foca Tactical Group or he had the authority to sign on behalf of the Tactical Group; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let it be so, because I do not know what is the state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher to give the B/C/S version back to the witness and have the English on the ELMO. The request was to use the premises within the KP Dom compound for the accommodation of prisoners of war, and it talks about the premises being used temporarily and that would they would be returned in good condition. Okay. I would like to have the witness now shown Exhibit D38/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: After you received that request, you wrote this response, right, and signed it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And it's dated the 10th of May, 1992, which means that's the day that you wrote it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 10th of May, 1992. That's what it says, so that's probably when it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The 10th of May, 1992 was a Sunday, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So you were --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what day it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The Prosecution has a calendar of May 1992 which shows that May 10th was, in fact, a Sunday, and I can show it to Defence counsel and see if they agree to that. This was something that was generated through the computer. I think, Your Honour, if we could just ask Mr. Bakrac or Mr. Vasic if they agree that in fact it's a Sunday so that we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm afraid you're speaking so quietly I didn't even hear you. I don't know whether the interpreters did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I wanted to know if Mr. Bakrac or Mr. Vasic had an objection to proceeding on the fact that May 10th, 1992, was a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on the -- this computer paper it says that that was the 10th. But it's 1.00 and perhaps a convenient time for a break. So we shall check it, compare it with our calculations, and if that is so, then no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll resume at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just before the break we were asking Defence counsel whether they would agree that May 10th, 1992 was a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So Mr. Krnojelac, you wrote that particular document, D38, on a Sunday; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't on Sunday, that's for sure. I told you: When I got the letter, I first consulted Mr. Mladjenovic, and after that, this document was written. And as for the calendar, I didn't have one in front of me, so it is possible that whoever was doing the actual writing made a mistake in the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You wrote that document, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote it, but couldn't it have been possible for me to write on Monday, the 11th, that it was the 10th, and then I had it typed and then -- obviously there was a mistake. I agree with you that the 10th is a Sunday, but I guarantee that I did not sign it on a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, let's have this document placed before you again. When you wrote this decision granting permission to the military to use premises of the KP Dom, you wrote that the premises were temporarily allocated for the accommodation of prisoners of war and detained persons.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The request was only for prisoners of war. You added the words "detained persons," didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what was in the request. However, since other persons were there as well, of Serb ethnicity, who were detained, then this was added to the former. I don't know what it said originally in the request, whether it was imprisoned persons and then detained persons too. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: All right. We'll have you given Exhibit D38 and you can take a look. The request is for accommodation of prisoners of war, full stop.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what it says. However, at that time, since there were also persons of Serb ethnicity who were detained, it is for that case that I added this, and that is why it says "prisoners of war and detained persons."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So you wrote a decision in which you gave the military accommodations for more than they actually requested; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I stated, together with Mr. Mladjenovic, president of the municipality, I said that there were detained persons as well, and then I'm sure he knew this, and he said, "Oh, just be free to write for both, because you have nothing to do with either of them, so they will both be put up there." So it is with his approval that I wrote this decision, because he then said to me, "What would be better accommodation than what we have right now at the KP Dom?"

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You, according to your testimony, met with Mr. Mladjenovic regarding the decision. You met with him over the weekend, right, because the 8th was a Friday.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely on the 8th. If it was a Friday, it is most probable that I consulted with him immediately, that I went to the municipality, carried out consultations, and on Monday finished this, because I did not want to do this on my own either.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You didn't have to get anyone else's signature on this; right? You didn't have to meet with Savo Todovic or Mitar Rasevic or Marko Kovac. You wrote this with your signature, right, and that was enough for the decision to take effect?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision for the temporary allocation of accommodation in agreement with the president of the Executive Committee, that was decided, and I thought there was no need for me to contact anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And there is no other document, no separate document that has Mr. Mladjenovic's signature granting permission to use the KP Dom. This is the only document granting permission and it has your signature on it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since at that time I was temporary warden, I asked him. He gave his approval to me. He did not give me any orders in writing or any other document in writing, only what you see here. As far as I can remember, only this, what you can see here. That is how it all ended.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You never spoke to the commander of the Foca Tactical Group about what specifically they were requesting, right, in terms of what particular premises and for how long and who would be in charge? You never had any meetings or contact with the military to get those details, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No meeting, nothing, except for this request that was submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And the decision that you made, that you signed, 38/1, that also doesn't specify what premises, for how long, and who would be in charge of those premises, does it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not specified. It just says that they have to maintain the premises and keep them in proper condition, return them in proper condition, but it was considered that these were quarters for detained persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher to have 38/1 placed on the ELMO. I'm sorry. The English translation is fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, according to your decision, it says the premises of the KP Dom Foca are temporarily allocated. It doesn't say a part of it, does it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The premises are temporarily allocated for the accommodation, the premises of the Foca Penal and Correctional Facility, the accommodation of prisoners of war and detained persons. This accommodation meant the premises where they were put up anyway at the moment when I arrived - I said that - on the 18th of May. So accommodation in those premises where they were already accommodated. That's what I meant, and that is exactly the way I view it today, that these are the premises where they were accommodated anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, can you explain to us why you needed to have this decision if they were accommodated there already?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, this paper, this request, and I did request this from Mr. Mladjenovic in a certain way, to have things known, whose is what, to have these people moved out. And then since he said that it was impossible to relocate them to another because there was no such facility, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the letter was sent, the decision was reached, this was obtained, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Are you saying that the Tactical Group commander wrote his request because you asked for the request to be made so there was something in writing?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot assert that. I can only assert that I said to Mr. Mladjenovic that in some way this should be regulated, and he said that he would certainly regulate it. And he did, or, rather, they did regulate it the way they regulated it, like this, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: There's nothing in this decision that says the guard building was allocated to the military, is there? That remained part of your jurisdiction; right? That's not where the accommodations of the prisoners of war and detained persons were.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, upon arriving at the KP Dom, this building was under the people who were from Uzice. And afterwards, it remained to be an auxiliary building for these premises, just like the dining hall, because these are auxiliary premises and one cannot function without the other. And the economic unit did not really need these buildings, so it did not affect it, the fact that this was allocated to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So these additional buildings, you're saying, were allocated for military use without a written decision, right, as auxiliary buildings, in your words?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were auxiliary buildings in relation to these buildings that pertain to the accommodation of people, and they were also taken before I came, except for the dining hall. The dining hall was not taken because it had not been prepared to function.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: There's nothing in this document, is there, Mr. Krnojelac, that says that these premises will be maintained by a separate staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the guard building or -- excuse me. What are you exactly referring to? I'm not sure I know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'm talking about the piece of paper in front of you, your decision to allocate the premises of the Foca KP Dom for the accommodation of prisoners of war and detained persons. There is nothing in this decision that you wrote and signed that says that these premises that are being allocated for this use would be maintained by a separate staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here very nicely: "The user of the premises is obliged to maintain them and return them in good condition." I mean by that that the user is who? It says up here the prisoners of war and detained persons. For me as a teacher, at that point that was quite sufficient for me. I'm not a lawyer, a legal person. It's not that I could explain this further or write something else. I thought this was sufficient, and I thought that that is what was meant by this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: There was nothing that says that there should be a separate staff that was in charge of that -- the part that was allocated to the military; right? It was the exact same staff at the KP Dom who were working in the part allocated to the military and the part that remained under your control as you describe it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I describe it, it is that staff that are there, precisely it is their duty to keep this in good condition. It is not for someone else to do that, no way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll move away from this document. Mr. Krnojelac, you testified earlier in your testimony that you had nothing to do with any weapons. You never carried weapons at the KP Dom, and you had absolutely nothing to do with them while you were at the KP Dom, and, "If you ask me," you said, "I'd burn all the weapons." Do you remember testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This last bit, I don't know if I said I'd burn it or use it as agricultural tools. But as for the rest, as far as I can remember, it's quite correct, because I think I even said that I would not even make toys for children that way, and I never carried weapons at the KP Dom, or anywhere else, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: But you were very much involved in the security of prisoners and detained persons, both within the KP Dom and when they were being transferred out; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Are you sure that you were never involved in a proposal to transfer prisoners and detained persons to -- or from Bileca?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never took part in that, I certainly didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have the witness shown Exhibit D39.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: This is a document which you signed, Mr. Krnojelac, dated 6th of May, 1993, and it's addressed to the Herzegovina Corps as well as the Foca Tactical Group, and it's a report regarding a proposal to relocate a prison from Bileca to Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And if we could move a little bit further down. Okay. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You talk about some of the problems that would be encountered in such a transfer, and you state in this order, or in this report, that: "In order to implement this order to transfer detainees from Bileca to Foca," and I emphasise the word "detainees," "we believe the following issues need to be resolved." And you talk about having to provide security, adequate security personnel. You list 20 employees securing the KP Dom who were sent as military conscripts, and then in addition, there were 24 other military conscripts, and you state: "This personnel structure does not meet even the most minimum requirements for this type of work, and we therefore believe that for the security of inmates, at least 30 workers with prior security experience need to be provided." So you made a report to the military, telling them exactly what you needed in order to carry out the security of a transfer of detainees to the KP Dom; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you, because -- I mean, I was listening to what you were saying, because you have a legible manuscript. But this report is an answer to a request by the Herzegovina Corps to relocate the prison from Bileca to Foca, the prison from Bileca to Foca, and down here, as far as I can see, the answer is quite different. Probably in this request of theirs I was actually answering that which should happen. However, here I am saying in this piece of information that since this institution falls under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice and administration of Republika Srpska, it is necessary to obtain their approval, that is to say, not my approval, but their approval, the approval of the ministry, in order to have this carried out and to do something like that, to relocate the prison from Bileca to Foca. That is not to say that I could decide this of my own free will, but they had to ask the Ministry of Justice for approval so that this could be done. So with your permission, I would like to say that this is a kind of answer to their request, because I did not have the right to do that, or rather, I had to ask my superiors, and that is, the Ministry of Justice, the ministry of the judiciary, and that is why I did not take part in this. And for as long as I was there, this was not even carried through, and I had to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: My question to you, Mr. Krnojelac, was not about your authority to approve this. I understand, and it's clear from the document, that they needed to get approval from the Ministry of Justice, but my question was simply your knowledge. You had a very detailed knowledge of exactly how many military conscripts were working for security, and you also had a very detailed knowledge of how many more would be needed for security purposes; isn't that right? Because that's what you put into the document.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, in agreement with my associates that I received such information from them, they who knew about this and that this was necessary and that I obtained this kind of information from them, and that is the kind of answer that I gave in respect of what was supposed to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'd like to have you shown Exhibit P446. This is a list signed by you; isn't that right, Mr. Krnojelac? It's your signature on the second page?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And are you able to read the date for us? It's a little bit difficult to see that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only see here October 1992. I cannot see any other date. Oh, yes, yes. Are you referring to the one that's written in pen or are you referring to the list of military conscripts on the first page, the date over there?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I mean the date --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The date of your signature, so it would be the second page. To the left of your signature it says -- it looks like 23 November nineteen-ninety something, and that last date is not clear on the handwritten copy. Are you able to make that out or tell us what date that was, what year?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not this, but over here, because it says on the first page for October 1992, it is probably also 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Okay. Then just for the record, the English translation which has it as 23 November 1997 is inaccurate. It should be 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, you testified during your direct examination that you were given this list and that you signed it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And if you look at the first page, you will see that it's listed as a list of men liable for military service, members of the Foca KP Dom, October 1992. And you are listed first and your rank is Captain First Class. Everybody else in the list after you is listed simply as a soldier. That's accurate; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it looks, yes: soldier, soldier, soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And among the people on the list, if you look at number 2, is Savo Todovic, and number 3, Mitar Rasevic, Relja Goljanin, Drakul Bozo, a lot of people that we've already talked about as working at the KP Dom at this time. And number 19, for example, it Risto Ivanovic, who was working as a guard at the KP Dom; right? This is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So you knew that all these people were liable for military service?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to their age. And up here it says military conscripts. And in terms of their age, I knew that they were subject to military obligation, because everybody under the age of 55 was eligible for military obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You prepared this list in preparation for the possible mobilisation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not prepare this list. I did not prepare it for mobilisation. I did not prepare it at all. At any rate, the main objective of this list was, as I said, the Ministry of Defence was supposed to know how many military conscripts were where, because I knew that that was done in other enterprises, other companies as well. I did not prepare this list, nor was such a unit with this composition, for as long as I was at the KP Dom, have any other purpose but working on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. information in terms of how many military conscripts there were, although some of them got military obligation and others got work obligation. And then afterwards, or perhaps even immediately then, an attempt was made to show in this way that these people were supposed to receive some parcels, and I thought that this was unfair, because there were other people who also worked at the KP Dom. So they were supposed to get them too. But this turned out to be a way of getting allowances or parcels from the military because they were military conscripts, men of military age.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So, Mr. Krnojelac, on the 23rd of November, 1992, when you signed this document, you knew the names of all the people who were working at the KP Dom who were eligible for military duty, including all the security guards; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I am telling you that I did sign this list, but I did not compile it. This list was literally compiled by Mr. Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I understand that you've told us that he compiled it, but it's your signature on it, not his, and therefore, you knew the names of these people; right? That was your responsibility before you sign a document, that you look it over, read it, and know its contents; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I am putting it to you that I only paid attention to the years of birth and none to the names. I did take care of the year of birth, because up there it says people liable for military duty, and that is why I paid attention to that, and I didn't pay attention to the rest, and that is what I said. Of course, the Honourable Court will take its decision. I cannot say anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You knew --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: -- Mr. Krnojelac, as of the 9th of June, 1992, exactly how many Muslim detainees were in the KP Dom; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I already told you in my testimony so far that from time to time, from time to time, now and then, I knew, I learnt the number of people from the man responsible for the warehouse, because when it came to food, then he would sometimes tell me, "Well, Milorad, there's so many of them."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You knew the exact number of people who had passed through the KP Dom as well; right? In other words, people that were brought there and then released. You knew that number as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You also knew how many military conscripts were working at the KP Dom as of June 9, 1992. That number was 42; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it only on the basis of one document, and at that time I did not know it, nor did I have an occasion or opportunity to know it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was the one document that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the one that you mention and in which 38 or I don't know how many people, because it is the document with my signature, and I did not deny that it was my signature, having to do with the mining, then that is it. And I apologise, because I admitted it to my Defence, that that was my signature, and we did not challenge that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You also knew, in June 1992, exactly how many weapons and what kind were available at the KP Dom; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know, but it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You -- this document that you're referring to was a document in which -- which you signed; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the same document, then, yes, if it's about mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And in the document, you requested that there be mines -- this was a letter to the War Presidency of the Serbian municipality of Foca in which you ask mines to be placed at the KP Dom; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, I should like to explain this. If you could also give me the document, I'd like to see it, and I can explain everything that I know about this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you first before we get to the document. You requested that mines be put into the KP Dom; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not request that mines be placed in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You never ever asked for mines to be placed in the KP Dom for security purposes?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For no reason, for no reason whatsoever did I ask the mines to be placed in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have the witness shown Exhibit P445.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, I would like to start first with the second page of this document and ask you if that is your signature and stamp.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Let's go to the first page then. This is a letter which you wrote and signed to the War Presidency of the Serbian municipality of Foca. It's dated 9th of June, and the letter talks about how you had -- the subject of the letter is a request for mine laying and weapon replacements. In your request, you state that on an earlier date, on the 1st of June, 1992, you submitted a request to the Crisis Staff asking for mines to be put down and that experts came to inspect the grounds and agreed with the recommendation but did not actually put the mines in, and that was the reason for this letter of the 9th of June, to get action; right? There was a previous request which was partially followed up on, but because it was not fully implemented, you sent this second request; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not send a request. I did say that I signed it. But a man who fell out of the blue, and I -- that was me who came to become the temporary warden of the penitentiary, reformatory, had I even been there for a longer time, I could never know any one of these items, because I did not have any documentation as to what -- how many people there were, how many people had passed through the KP Dom by then and that I should know how many military conscripts -- how many conscripts should guard those men. This could be written only by a man who had exact information as to how many people had passed through, how many people there were in the KP Dom at the time, how many persons were needed to guard them. Because I am a teacher. How can I know how many people are needed to guard and what their number -- what the necessary number is? I couldn't possibly know that. So this paper was put on my desk, and I was -- it was said, "Milorad, this is a paper you should sign." Why? In order to put mines in the upper part where it says there are no lights and where there are no guards. And incidentally, to protect the property, because that upper part that is along the KP Dom was unprotected, and because it was also sent from the command to sign it. Mr. Savo Todovic brought this to me, and at that moment, as the temporary warden, without any knowledge about this, that is what I put to you, I signed it, and because he said that that was the only way in which the unit could enter and lay the mines. But they did not put the -- did not put the mines only where it says here in the upper part, they also, unfortunately, that is, alongside the upper part of the fence, on the upper part of the Dom, they also laid those mines, or, rather, not afterwards, but that same day, they also laid the mines in the lower part, in the lower part which did not have any asphalt covering, in the direction of the warehouse where the stocks of the furniture factory were kept. And that is why I say that I'm not competent to say, to give my opinion about this, nor did I have all these elements with me, nor did I know anything about this until that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, you're saying that Savo Todovic prepared this request?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He brought it to me so that I would sign it, and I personally think that only the military could know, and he perhaps, and perhaps the guard commander, how many weapons there are in a group. He brought it to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. me to sign it. Whether he wrote it, I cannot say that, because I did not see him do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Surely you read the document before putting your signature on it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I read the document, yes, I did. I can't say I didn't, because it would be foolish to sign something without reading it first, and I did not think there was anything bad about it for those people who were in the penitentiary, reformatory. I did not think it was an aggravating circumstance. I thought it was a security element. And because of the property, because above the quarters of the KP Dom is the part where there is a factory, and that is where the central warehouse was and the production materials for that factory and so on and so forth, in that upper part precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, it would also be foolish to sign something if you didn't agree with it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you how was it that I signed it, because the security in this upper part and the property itself in the KP Dom. Because it was not lit, there was no outside security. I think it was quite clear when we said that there is the inside security and the outside security. In that part there was no outside security, according to his explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, you've told us today that your reason for requesting the mines to be laid down was that it was protection for the property that was in that area, but there's nothing in this request that makes any reference whatsoever to property, is there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is something here, somewhere where it says that this upper part is not lit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: There is the sentence in paragraph 3, at the second half, where you say: "This is especially relevant, in view of the fact that there is no lighting along the perimeter wall or on the premises of the institution. We have been informed recently that a number of detained persons might try to escape from the institution." So the reason that was given was a fear of escape by the detained persons; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you that I did not write this and I didn't quote this as a reason. I did not write it, but signed it, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And by signing it, you agreed with it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
